{"candidates":[{"name":"strict_explicit_final_cta","prompt":"You are grading an e-commerce product description written by an AI copywriter. Check exactly one criterion: **the description ends with a call to action (CTA).**

Criterion definition: The last paragraph or section of the output is a clear call to action that urges the buyer to purchase or try the product, and no other content follows it.

Apply a STRICT reading:
1. Find the very last piece of non-whitespace content in the output. Ignore trailing whitespace only.
2. That final content must be an explicit, direct CTA. It should use imperative wording that tells the reader to buy, order, add to cart, shop, get, grab, or try the product. Examples: "Add it to your cart today", "Order yours now", "Shop the set today and...". A sentence that only summarizes benefits or praises the product (e.g., "This set gives you everything you need") is NOT a CTA. Neither is a vague aspiration (e.g., "Elevate your style") unless it clearly urges purchase or trial.
3. Nothing may come after the CTA. FAIL if the CTA is followed by any other content, such as another heading, more feature or benefit text, a disclaimer, notes, keyword lists, SEO metadata, word counts, or commentary addressed to the user.
4. FAIL if the output appears truncated or cut off, for example ending mid-sentence or mid-word. A truncated output cannot end with a CTA.
5. A CTA inside the last section is fine, even if that section has a heading such as "Why Choose..." or "Order Today", but the CTA sentence has to be the final sentence of the whole output.
6. FAIL if there is no CTA at all, or if the only CTA appears earlier in the text instead of at the end.

Imperative phrasing about buying or getting the product counts, e.g., "Add to cart", "Order today", "Get yours now", "Pick up a set and start creating", "Try it today". Softer phrasing also counts if it clearly directs the reader toward purchasing or trying, e.g., "Make it part of your routine today." A purely descriptive summary with no push to act does NOT count.
- The CTA must be the last meaningful content. FAIL if more product content comes after it, such as new features, benefits, another subheading with body text, notes to the user, SEO keyword lists, or word counts. Trailing whitespace or a closing punctuation mark is fine.

candidates.name: strict_explicit_final_cta
candidates.prompt:
You are grading an e-commerce product description written by an AI copywriter. Check exactly one criterion: **the description ends with a call to action (CTA).**

Criterion definition: The last paragraph or section of the output is a clear call to action that urges the buyer to purchase or try the product, and no other content follows it.

Apply a STRICT reading:
1. Find the very last piece of non-whitespace content in the output. Ignore trailing whitespace only.
2. That final content must be an explicit, direct CTA. It should use imperative wording that tells the reader to buy, order, add to cart, shop, get, grab, or try the product. Examples: "Add it to your cart today", "Order yours now", "Shop the set today and...". A sentence that only summarizes benefits or praises the product (e.g., "This set gives you everything you need") is NOT a CTA. Neither is a vague aspiration (e.g., "Elevate your style") unless it clearly urges purchase or trial.
3. Nothing may come after the CTA. FAIL if the CTA is followed by any other content, such as another heading, more feature or benefit text, a disclaimer, notes, keyword lists, SEO metadata, word counts, or commentary addressed to the user.
4. FAIL if the output appears truncated or cut off, for example ending mid-sentence or mid-word. A truncated output cannot end with a CTA.
5. A CTA inside the last section is fine, even if that section has a heading such as "Why Choose..." or "Order Today", but the CTA sentence has to be the final sentence of the whole output.
6. FAIL if there is no CTA at all, or if the only CTA appears earlier in the text instead of at the end.

Pipeline inputs (for context only):
{inputs}

Output to judge:
<<<
{output}
>>>

Respond with a JSON object only: {"pass": true|false, "reason": "<one or two sentences quoting the final sentence and explaining your decision>"}. pass=true means the output satisfies the criterion: it ends with an explicit purchase/try call to action and nothing follows it. pass=false means it does not.
